subject: Access patterns, endpoint mapping and hosted feasibility — post-demo follow-up
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Voss <samira@finlytics.io>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Aug 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Access patterns, endpoint mapping and hosted feasibility — post-demo follow-up

Thanks again for the demo time today — appreciated the walkthrough, Samira and Dan. Quick recap and a few clarifying asks so we can scope the recommended onramp path (Hosted API pilot vs Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC).

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary use: real-time summarization + customer-facing recommendations inside FinLytics web app.
- Expected steady traffic: low single-digit RPS per endpoint, but daily report windows may spike.
- Data sensitivity: some PII in logs; FinLytics compliance team will confirm retention rules.

Clarifying questions for sizing & deployment recommendation
1) Traffic profile: can you share a short CSV with average RPS by hour and 95th percentile request size? (I attached a sample CSV for the format.)
2) Latency SLO: you mentioned p95 desirable target — can you confirm target (e.g., <=300ms p95)?
3) Compliance constraints: do you require customer-managed keys or a VPC-only control plane for initial pilot?
4) Failover expectations: is a cross-region fallback acceptable, or must traffic remain in a single region?

What we recommend for a fast pilot (if compliance & keys allow)
- Hosted API sandbox: staging endpoint and API key for quick integration (2–3 business days).
- Default ratecaps for pilot: we can start with 50 req/s (burst to 100 for short windows); we can tune based on the provided traffic CSV.
- Endpoint mapping: map 1 sandbox endpoint per major feature (summarize, recommend) to preserve cache locality and KV prefixes.
- Observability: we'll enable token-level cost & latency dashboards for the pilot and a canary route for safe rollout.

If the compliance team needs private networking / KMS, next step is a short checklist we can route to our Privacy & Security team to scope Dedicated vs Private VPC. That process typically takes 1–2 weeks to finalize controls.

Next steps I propose
- Samira/Daniel: share the traffic CSV and confirm p95 latency target and KMS/VPC requirement (reply below).
- Redwood: we’ll provision a sandbox endpoint and share a quickstart playbook + SOC2 summary (attached) and a proposed mutual action plan.
- Schedule: technical deep-dive with FinLytics SRE + Redwood SE to validate network/egress needs — available Fri 10–11am PT or Mon afternoon.

Attachments: finlytics-traffic-sample.csv (format), redwood-quickstart-playbook.pdf, redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
From: Samira Voss <samira@finlytics.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@finlytics.io>
Date: Wed, 1 Aug 2028 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Access patterns, endpoint mapping and hosted feasibility — post-demo follow-up

Thanks, Irene — great summary. A few quick answers below inline.

> 1) Traffic profile: can you share a short CSV...
We’ll attach a 7-day sample traffic export (hourly) in my reply. Expect ~10–12 RPS steady across core endpoints, spikes up to ~40 RPS during batch report windows (roughly 20 minutes, twice per day). Average request payload is ~600 tokens.

> 2) Latency SLO: confirm target
Target: p95 < 300ms ideally; p99 < 800ms is acceptable for some background flows.

> 3) Compliance constraints: KMS/VPC required?
Short-term pilot: hosted is preferred for speed to value — we want to start there if SOC2 evidence + IP allowlisting can be provided. Long term: FinLytics legal is leaning to a Private VPC with customer-managed keys for production. We’ll need an evaluation to decide before a full rollout.

> 4) Failover expectations
Single-region is preferred for data residency, but cross-region fallback is fine for non-sensitive workloads.

Can you send sandbox credentials and the quickstart playbook? Also please include the SOC2 summary for our security review. We’d like to schedule the SE deep-dive Friday 10am PT.

Regards,
Samira Voss
Product Lead, Integrations | FinLytics
samira@finlytics.io

-----Original message-----
On Wed, 1 Aug 2028 at 15:12, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo time today — appreciated the walkthrough, Samira and Dan. Quick recap and a few clarifying asks so we can scope the recommended onramp path (Hosted API pilot vs Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC).
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Voss <samira@finlytics.io>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Aug 2028 18:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Access patterns, endpoint mapping and hosted feasibility — post-demo follow-up

Great — thanks for the quick answers, Samira. Action items from our side and timeline: 

1) Sandbox provisioning (Irene/Rachel) — we will provision a staging API key and two sandbox endpoints (summarize + recommend) by EOD Thursday. We’ll set pilot ratecaps to 50 req/s with short bursts to 100, and we’ll open a support ticket to raise limits if the traffic sample shows higher sustained spikes.

2) Security artifacts — attaching the SOC2 summary (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf). If FinLytics needs a certified letter or additional attestations we can route a request to our compliance team.

3) Mutual action plan & next meeting — I’ll push a one-page MAP into the Google Drive folder and propose Fri 10–11am PT for the SE + SRE deep-dive. Agenda: network egress, IP allowlist, KMS options and quickstart integration checklist.

4) Endpoint mapping recommendation — for the pilot we recommend separate endpoints per user-facing feature to allow per-endpoint rate limits and more effective prefix/KV caching. We’ll include an example mapping in the playbook.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
